description: attn's tools for the work you share with the user and the agents beside you. Reach for them to track, report or hand off work, and before you tell the user attn can't do something.
instructions:
attn runs you beside the user's other agents. These tools are attn's. Each tool's description holds its rules: read it before the first call. Find a tool by the words in this map.

| When you need to | Tools |
|---|---|
| See what each agent is doing right now, or reset one session's line | activity, activity_clear |
| Message, watch or close other agents; read your inbox | agent_msg, agent_peek, agent_close, agent_inbox |
| Point at something in the app for the user | callout_anchors, callout_show |
| Start another agent on work you may hand off, and follow its start | delegate, delegate_status |
| Read or change the models and harnesses each delegation role uses | delegate_roles, delegate_roles_set, delegate_roles_history, delegate_roles_rollback |
| Answer the user's questions about attn from the user guide | guide |
| List every session and profile | list |
| Set up code navigation in a review for a language with no working server | nav_status, nav_check, nav_set |
| Show or finish the Chief's onboarding | onboarding |
| Show the user a markdown document or a seed in a tile | open |
| Present a change for the user to review, or answer their question on it | review_start, review_check, review_answer |
| Find work you can pick up, read a seed or plan, claim it | seed_ready, seed_show, seed_tend |
| Record progress or prove a check on a seed you tend | seed_note, seed_check_report |
| Finish, pause, abandon or give back a seed | seed_harvest, seed_park, seed_wither, seed_replant |
| Track new work, find existing work, split a plan | seed_search, seed_plant, seed_plot, seed_link |
| Change a seed's body, checks, files or reminders | seed_edit, seed_check_add, seed_attach, seed_remind |
| Wait for a time, a pull request or another seed, with your session closed | seed_standby |
| Read past sessions, or rename or snooze a session | session_list, session_transcript, session_rename, session_snooze, session_unsnooze |
| Read the rules for an attn capability before you first use it | skill |
| Find out why a session shows the state it does | state_explain |
| Bring the user to you after a notification run | turn_open |
| Report what got in your way | vent |

A seed is one unit of work in the garden, with an id like s-7k3f9m, a slug made of its title's words, a markdown body, checks (C1, C2) and a log. A plot is a seed with children. Tools take the id or the slug. Give other agents the id, because a slug two seeds share is refused. To the user, say the slug.

Track work that outlives this turn in seeds, not in TODO lists: they end with the session. Search before you plant, and plant before you start. Write every body as a work prompt for an agent who has not seen this conversation. Harvest a seed when the outcome and the verification its body asks for are complete.

An update about a seed asks you to read what changed, not to act. Act only when the update needs you or the user.
name: attn

tools.name: activity
tools.title: what each agent is doing, and why nothing is generated
tools.description: Shows whether activity lines are generated and why not when they are not: the presence tier (nothing is generated while nobody can see it), the setting, and whether an agent is chosen to write them. Then each session that generates a line, with its line, its age and why its last run failed.

tools.name: activity_clear
tools.title: forget one session's line and its read position
tools.description: Forgets one session's activity line and its read position, so the next line is written from what happens next.

id.description: the full id of the session

tools.name: agent_list
tools.title: the address book of every session on this daemon
tools.description: The address book: every session on this daemon with its short id, name, profile, state, and whether a turn is owed. Inside attn it lists your session's profile. Read-only.

tools.name: agent_peek
tools.title: observe a session without interrupting it
tools.description: Observes a session without interrupting it: state, last assistant message, and the rendered screen. On a Claude session, says when the composer holds Claude's suggestion and not typed text. Passive: the observed agent never notices. `target` is a crew name, a full session id, or a unique session id prefix. A crew member between sessions stays between sessions.

target.description: a crew name, full session id, or unique id prefix

tools.name: agent_msg
tools.title: send a session, crew member or seed a message
tools.description: Sends a session, crew member or seed a message. The body stays in the inbox; the recipient gets a generic inbox notification. A target that cannot take input safely keeps it queued. The result says queued, notified, or refused. attn starts a session for a member between sessions before the notification is placed. A seed id reaches its current or next tender, waiting when none is reachable. In the CLI, a message that starts with - goes after --, as: attn agent msg -- <target> "-text".

target.description: a session id or unique prefix, a crew member's name, or a seed id

tools.name: agent_close
tools.title: close a session for good, with a reason
tools.description:
Closes a session for good. A session may close itself and agents below it in its delegation chain, including delegates of delegates; the profile's Chief may close any agent of that profile. The reason is required: the session row stays in the ledger, and the reason is what the next reader gets. Without `compact` it is immediate, so say what you have to say first. A seed id closes whoever tends it, and the seed keeps its tender with a note about the close. `self` closes the caller without its id and takes no target.

`compact` goes only with `self`: attn waits for your turn to end, compacts your conversation through the harness, then closes the session. End your turn right after: you get no turn after the compact. When the compact fails, the session still closes, and the reason says the compact did not run. Only a Claude session with the Claude mod and a Codex session on the shared Codex app server compact, on the home machine or an outpost, and a Sigma session on the home machine; attn refuses any other session and says why. Compact only a session that will resume as itself, as a seed's tender does when its standby resumes it. A crew member's next session starts fresh.

compact.description: compact the conversation after this turn, then close (with self)

target.description: the session id or unique prefix, or the seed whose tender to close

tools.name: agent_reload
tools.title: interrupt and reload agents in place
tools.description: Interrupts and reloads agents in place, as "Reload this agent" does. Running work is interrupted and non-persistent state may be lost. Full ids, unique prefixes and names of crew members in session work; a member between sessions stays between sessions. A member whose saved harness matches its session reloads with its saved model and effort. A session may reload itself and descendants; the profile's chief may reload any agent in that profile. `all` is chief-only, includes the chief and crew, and excludes shells. Chief and crew close protections do not prevent reload. Each target reports an outcome; failures leave successful reloads in place. Repeated targets reload once. Exited agents use 80x24. The caller reloads last if selected; a self reload may interrupt the command before its result arrives.

all.description: every agent in the caller's profile (chief only)

targets.description: the sessions or crew members to reload

tools.name: agent_inbox
tools.title: read your unread notifications, or one message by id
tools.description: Reads up to 20 unread notifications in FIFO order, or one notified user or peer message by `message`. Each returned item gets its durable read receipt. `limit` can be 1 through 50.

limit.description: how many unread items to read (default 20)

tools.name: agent_msg_status
tools.title: whether a message you sent is queued, notified or read
tools.description: Inspects a message you sent as queued, notified, or read.

tools.name: agent_attachment
tools.title: download a file the user attached to a message
tools.description: Downloads a saved user file from this session's profile to `out`, then you can inspect it. Outside a session, choose the profile when more than one profile exists.

capture.description: the quick capture the file came with

out.description: where to write the file; it must not exist yet; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

tools.name: callout_anchors
tools.title: list the anchors and which are on screen
tools.description: Lists every anchor with its description, and for each fixed anchor whether it is on screen now. Run it before `callout_show` to pick an anchor the user can see. When the app is not showing your profile, the list still comes back with `app_showing_profile` false and no anchor marked on screen.

tools.name: callout_show
tools.title: show a callout the user steps through
tools.description: Shows a callout: each step's text beside its anchor, in order. Put the agent or desktop the user should go to on the last step, because Enter and → go there only from the last step. If a fixed anchor is missing, the whole callout is refused and the message names the anchors on screen. A new callout replaces the one showing. The call returns when the app accepts the callout.

steps.description: each step's anchor and its text, at most 20 steps of at most 160 characters

anchor.description: A fixed anchor such as garden, agent:<who> or desktop:<which>.

tools.name: delegate
tools.title: start another agent on work you may hand off
tools.description:
Starts another agent in its own session, which the user can open and steer. Every delegation has a seed, which the delegated agent reads when it starts: `brief` plants a new one, and `seed` uses an existing seed's current assignment. `handover` transfers that seed to the new agent, with `note` as the next step; the previous agent keeps running. `authorization` says how far the user lets the task go, written as instructions to the agent; it is saved on the seed, and the opening delivers it. Without it, a delegation keeps the seed's current words.

`model` is required unless `role` or `fallback` picks the model from the user's delegation roles (`delegate_roles` lists them). `cwd` is the folder or repository on the target machine, `host` or the caller's own. Inside Git, choose one complete checkout: `reuse_checkout` with `branch`, `new_worktree` with `branch` and `from`, or `new_worktree` with `existing_branch`. Outside Git, `cwd` is enough. On the caller's own machine, a relative `cwd` resolves against the CLI's working directory, or the folder a tool caller's session started in. Only a handover's predecessor is exempt from checkout occupancy; any other active session there needs `allow_worktree_reuse`.

A tool call answers with the operation once attn accepts the request, and `delegate_status` reads it later; the CLI waits until the agent has started and prints its result. Pass the same `request_id` to retry safely: a retry returns the accepted operation instead of starting another.

agent.description: a configured prompt-capable agent (default: the caller's)

allow_worktree_reuse.description: share a checkout another active session uses

authorization.description: how far the user lets this task go, written as instructions to the agent; saved on the seed

branch.description: the branch to reuse, or the new branch to create

brief.description: the task: plants a seed for new work

cwd.description: the folder or repository on that machine (required)

desktop.description: a desktop of your profile for the new agent: its shortcut digit (1-9), its name or its id; the agent opens at the end of that desktop's row without changing what you see (default: the caller's desktop)

effort.description: pin the effort; "default" selects the harness default (default: medium where supported)

existing_branch.description: a local branch for the new worktree

fallback.description: the configured model for work no role fits

from.description: the ref a new branch starts from

handover.description: transfer the seed to the new agent

host.description: the outpost to run on, by name or id; home selects the home (default: the caller's machine)

model.description: pin the model; "default" selects the harness default

name.description: the session's name, at most 48 characters (default: from the brief or the seed's title)

note.description: the handover note: the next step

priority.description: put the delegate's owed turns first

provider.description: the provider for a plugin harness model; with role or fallback

request_id.description: a stable retry key; op- is reserved (default: a new one, which the CLI prints)

reuse_checkout.description: use the checkout at cwd on branch

role.description: a configured delegation role, with its default choice

seed.description: an existing seed whose assignment the agent takes

yolo.description: launch the agent with its approval prompts bypassed

tools.name: delegate_status
tools.title: a delegation's operation, by request or operation id
tools.description: Reads a delegation's operation by its request id or operation id: its state, its progress, the session it started, and its result once it has one.

id.description: the request id or operation id

tools.name: delegate_roles
tools.title: the roles agents choose from when delegating
tools.description: Prints the roles agents choose from when delegating: each role that is turned on and has a complete default model, its alternatives with when to pick them, and the fallback for work no role fits.

tools.name: delegate_roles_show
tools.title: the whole saved table, or one role's full guidance
tools.description: Answers the whole saved table: roles turned off, roles that still need a model, alternatives and the fallback. With `role`, also answers that role with its full guidance and alternatives, a maintained role's included. The table in the result is what `delegate_roles_apply` takes.

role.description: the role to read in full

tools.name: delegate_roles_history
tools.title: revisions of the table, newest first
tools.description: Lists revisions of the table newest first, with who changed what and why.

tools.name: delegate_roles_install
tools.title: add Attn's maintained roles the table lacks, and the skill they follow
tools.description: Adds Attn's maintained roles the table lacks, turns the table and its roles on, and installs the attn-workflow skill they follow for every available harness. Your roles stay. When one of yours already uses an Attn role's id, the Attn role gets a numeric suffix, such as builder-2.

tools.name: delegate_roles_add
tools.title: add a custom role, a maintained role, or an alternative model for a role
tools.description: Adds a role, or an alternative model for a role when `target` is role/alternative. A custom role needs `name`, and its default model comes from the model args. With `builtin`, the role is one of Attn's maintained roles: pathfinder, builder, reviewer, orchestrator or prototyper (`delegate_roles_install` must run once first). An alternative starts from the role's default model; `when` says when an agent should pick it instead of the default, and without a condition it is saved but never picked.

agent.description: the harness; changing it starts a fresh selection

builtin.description: make the role one of Attn's maintained roles

description.description: what the role is for (custom roles only)

effort.description: the effort; "default" selects the harness default

instructions.description: what the delegated agent is told to do (custom roles only)

model.description: the model; "default" selects the harness default

provider.description: the provider for a plugin harness model

when.description: when an agent should pick this alternative instead of the default

tools.name: delegate_roles_set
tools.title: change a role, one of its alternatives, or the fallback
tools.description: Changes a role, or one of its alternatives when `target` is role/alternative. `default` makes the alternative the role's default. With `fallback`, changes the model agents use when no role fits, and its `instructions`.

agent.description: the harness; changing it starts a fresh selection

default.description: make the alternative the role's default

description.description: what the role is for (custom roles only)

effort.description: the effort; "default" selects the harness default

fallback.description: change the fallback for work no role fits

instructions.description: what the delegated agent is told to do (custom roles only), or the fallback's instructions

model.description: the model; "default" selects the harness default

provider.description: the provider for a plugin harness model

when.description: when an agent should pick this alternative instead of the default

tools.name: delegate_roles_copy
tools.title: an editable custom copy of a role
tools.description: Makes an editable custom copy of a role, maintained ones included, placed after it in the table.

name.description: the copy's name (default: the role's name with (custom))

tools.name: delegate_roles_rm
tools.title: remove a role or one of its alternatives
tools.description: Removes a role, or one of its alternatives when `target` is role/alternative.

tools.name: delegate_roles_enable
tools.title: turn a role on, or the whole table
tools.description: Turns `role` on. Without a role, turns the whole table on.

tools.name: delegate_roles_disable
tools.title: turn a role off, or the whole table
tools.description: Turns `role` off. Without a role, turns the whole table off, and agents choose harness and model themselves.

tools.name: delegate_roles_apply
tools.title: replace the whole table with an exported one
tools.description: Replaces the whole table with `table`, the table `delegate_roles_show` returned. Refused when the table changed since that export.

table.description: the table, as delegate_roles_show returns it

tools.name: delegate_roles_rollback
tools.title: restore an earlier or later revision of the table
tools.description: With no `revision`, restores the table that was live before the current one; repeat to keep walking back. With `revision`, restores that one, older or newer: rolling forward is restoring a later revision.

revision.description: the revision to restore, as delegate_roles_history lists it

tools.name: guide
tools.title: read the user guide
tools.description: Prints the user guide's index: each page's topic, title and outline. `topic` prints one page instead, with its diagrams drawn as text. Use it to answer the user's questions about attn. `attn --help` lists commands.

topic.description: the page to print, as the index names it

tools.name: list
tools.title: list sessions and profiles
tools.description: Lists every session on this daemon and every profile, as JSON.

tools.name: nav_status
tools.title: the server definitions for a repository and the servers running here
tools.description: The server definitions for the repository in `repository`, where each program was found or why it was not, and the language servers running on this machine with their memory and, for one still starting, when its start began.

repository.description: a directory inside the repository; defaults to the current directory, or for a tool the folder the session started in; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

tools.name: nav_check
tools.title: resolve a definition on a line, starting the server when it is not running
tools.description: Asks for the definition of each name on the line `at`, in order, and answers with the first that resolves. Starts the server when it is not running. Setup is done when this resolves a real definition. Called as a tool, a server still starting after 20 s answers `starting` with the time so far and keeps starting: call again, and a running server answers at once. On the CLI the command waits for the answer.

at.description: a file relative to the repository and a line in it, such as internal/daemon/review.go:42

repository.description: a directory inside the repository; defaults to the current directory, or for a tool the folder the session started in; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

tools.name: nav_link
tools.title: link a server's program into this machine's code navigation folder
tools.description: Links the server's program at `program` into this machine's code navigation folder, which attn searches before PATH. Use it for a server your editor installed outside PATH, such as Neovim's mason folder. `as` links it under the name the definition's command uses.

as.description: the name to link it as; the program's file name by default

program.description: the server's program; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

tools.name: nav_unlink
tools.title: remove a link
tools.description: Removes the link `name` from this machine's code navigation folder.

name.description: the linked name, as `nav_status` lists it

tools.name: nav_set
tools.title: set how to launch the server for a language
tools.description: Sets how to launch the server for `language` in the repositories with this repository's origin. Outposts with a clone use it too. `definition` is JSON, such as {"command": ["jdtls"], "extensions": [".java"], "roots": ["MODULE.bazel"], "settings": {}, "prepare": {"command": ["tools/ide/setup_classpath.py"], "inputs": ["**/BUILD.bazel", "MODULE.bazel"]}}. command and extensions are required. roots are files that mark a workspace folder. settings go to the server at start. prepare runs from the workspace folder before the server starts, and again before a start once a file its inputs match has changed.

language.description: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, such as java

repository.description: a directory inside the repository; defaults to the current directory, or for a tool the folder the session started in; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

tools.name: nav_rm
tools.title: remove the definition set for a language
tools.description: Removes the definition set for `language`, so the built-in one applies again.

language.description: the language whose set definition goes

repository.description: a directory inside the repository; defaults to the current directory, or for a tool the folder the session started in; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

tools.name: onboarding
tools.title: whether the Chief's onboarding is pending, and which path it takes
tools.description: Shows whether the Chief's onboarding is pending, and which path it takes: the full path for a new user, or the tour for a user who used attn before the Chief.

tools.name: onboarding_done
tools.title: mark onboarding finished
tools.description: Marks the Chief's onboarding finished. `onboarding_again` runs the full path again.

tools.name: onboarding_again
tools.title: start the full path again in the Chief's next session
tools.description: Starts the full path again in the Chief's next session. It doesn't wake the Chief. An awake Chief can run it, then start the full path in its current conversation.

tools.name: open
tools.title: show the user a markdown document or a seed in a tile
tools.description: Opens the markdown file at `path`, or the seed `seed` (pass one of the two), in a tile next to your session. The tile reloads whenever the file changes. A review document's problems come back as `problems`; the tile opens anyway.

path.description: the markdown file to show; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

seed.description: the seed to show, by its id

tools.name: review_start
tools.title: snapshot the working tree as head and write the review's frontmatter
tools.description: Snapshots the working tree of `repository` as head, and writes frame (brief unless the document already picks one), repository, base and head into the frontmatter of `document`. Creates the document when it is missing, and leaves the text below the frontmatter as written. Run it again before presenting a revision: it takes a fresh head and keeps the base. `base` defaults to the head of the last review the user sent on this document, else the document's base; without one the review is a tour of unchanged code.

base.description: the commit the change is drawn against

document.description: the review document; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

repository.description: a directory inside the repository under review; defaults to the current directory, or for a tool the folder the session started in; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

tools.name: review_check
tools.title: list the document's problems, each with its line and the fix
tools.description: Lists the problems of `document`, each with its line and the fix. An empty list means the document is ready to open. On the CLI it exits 1 when there are problems, and `attn open` prints the same problems as warnings.

document.description: the review document; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

tools.name: review_answer
tools.title: answer a question the user asked on the review
tools.description: Answers a question the user asked on the review. The question arrives as the user's message with this command and the question's id; the answer shows under the line in the user's review.

document.description: the review document the question is on; a relative path resolves against the folder the session started in

question.description: the question's id, as the user's message gives it

text.description: the answer, a sentence or two that stands under the line

tools.name: seed_search
tools.title: find seeds by words, closed ones included
tools.description: Finds seeds by words across your profile's garden, harvested and withered included: titles, bodies and log entries. Words match as stemmed prefixes; identifier parts match too. Seeds carrying some words also appear. Ranks by title coverage, word coverage, relevance and recency, with a boost for open seeds. Prints status, last active and an original matching line. Search before you plant, so a duplicate is found instead of created.

limit.description: how many hits to answer with (default 10, at most 1000)

tools.name: seed_plant
tools.title: plant a seed and print its id, slug and title
tools.description: Plants a seed and prints its id, slug and title. `body` takes markdown; if the seed gains children, that body is the plot's plan. `part_of` plants it under a plot. `checks` defines what the seed must prove; attn numbers each check unless C#= names the id, and prints each id. Lists up to 3 similar open seeds in your profile, leaving out that plot. Planting always proceeds. If one is the same work, wither the new seed.

checks.description: a check the seed must prove; attn picks the id unless C#= names it; repeats

discovered_from.description: record the seed this work came from

tools.name: seed_plot
tools.title: plant a whole plot in one move from a JSON payload
tools.description:
Plants a whole plot in one move from a JSON payload, read from the `plot` file, or from stdin when the file is - or omitted: {"title": …, "body": …, "checks": [{"id": "C5", "text": …, "shared": true}], "part_of": "<plot>", "discovered_from": "<seed>", "children": [{"title": …, "body": …, "checks": […], "after": ["<sibling step slug>"]}]}.

Children are parallel by default; `after` names the siblings a child waits for, by step slug or full title. `part_of` plants the plot inside another plot, and `discovered_from` records the seed whose work turned up the plot; give each by id or slug. A shared check is proven by each seed below the plot that has no children. The plot, its children and their edges commit together. Prints the plot's id and each child's id and step slug, then up to 3 similar open seeds across all planted titles, each naming the new seed it resembles. Planting always proceeds; wither a new seed if a suggestion is the same work.

plot.description: the plot payload to read; - or omitted reads stdin

after.description: The siblings this child waits for, by step slug or full title.

discovered_from.description: The seed whose work turned up this plot, by id or slug.

part_of.description: A plot to plant this plot under, by id or slug.

tools.name: seed_link
tools.title: relate two seeds
tools.description: Relates two seeds. "a blocks b" keeps b out of ready until a closes. "a part-of b" puts a under b; b is then a plot. "a discovered-from b" records where work came from without ordering it. A structural cycle is refused, naming both seeds and the edge to remove.

a.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

b.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

tools.name: seed_unlink
tools.title: remove an edge between two seeds
tools.description: Removes the edge "a relation b". Every link has an unlink.

a.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

b.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

tools.name: seed_ready
tools.title: what you can tend right now
tools.description: Lists what you can tend right now, oldest first: nothing open blocks it, nobody is holding it, and it is not a plot, because a plot's work is its children. With neither `plot` nor `all` the scope is your profile's garden, unless this session was dispatched at a plot, and then that plot; `all` steps back out to the garden.

all.description: the whole garden, overriding a dispatched session's plot

tools.name: seed_ls
tools.title: the garden, newest first, with children nested under their plot
tools.description: Lists the garden, newest first, with children nested under their plot, without bodies or checks; `seed_show` reads one seed whole. `plot` lists every child of one plot, oldest first, harvested and withered included. `stale` narrows to open seeds whose log has not moved for `window` (default 7d): a query for your judgment, never a reaper. `standby` narrows to seeds on standby, each with the pull requests it watches and their readiness, its reminder, and why a resume is blocked when one is.

plot.description: list every child of this plot

stale.description: only open seeds whose log has not moved

tools.name: seed_show
tools.title: one seed, news first
tools.description:
Reads one seed, news first: its state, who tends it and a bookmark; the newest entries on its log, and where the freshest handoff is when it is older than those; every edge that touches it, with seeds discovered from it folded to a count and the open ones; the outline of the plot it is part of; a plot's open children as a board, each with what it waits for, its checks and its newest entry, closed children folded into one line; checks and artifacts; the body last.

`since` returns only the log entries saved after a bookmark, on this seed and every seed below it, newest first and labeled by seed, then a new bookmark. `section` returns one part of the body: the section under a heading, or every item that starts with an id like D3.

section.description: only the body's section under this heading (exact, or its start), or the items that start with this id, like D3

seed.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

since.description: only the log entries saved after the bookmark an earlier read printed, on this seed and every seed below it

tools.name: seed_notes
tools.title: the whole log, newest first
tools.description: Lists the whole log, newest first; `seed_show` renders the newest few and says how many more are here. A withered seed must be replanted first. A plot refuses while any direct child is open. A seed with an ask the user has not answered refuses and names the ask: end your turn, harvest after you act on the answer, or withdraw the ask with `attn ask close`. Closing a plot's last child leaves a ringing note on the plot and names the plot in the output. Moves print who they rang.

`when_merged` releases your claim and harvests the seed with your `reason` when the pull request merges. Without a reason it uses "PR #N merged: <title>". This command merges nothing. With no `pr` it takes this session's single open pull request, and names the pull requests when there is more than one; `when_merged` with `clear` takes the arming back.

tools.title: watch this seed and its descendants
tools.description: Subscribes this session to the seed and its descendants, including children planted later. Delegation starts the same watch on the seed it binds. Tending a plot already covers its descendants until the claim ends. A crew member's watch belongs to the member and lasts across the member's sessions. `seed_show` names the subscriptions that still cover a seed. Restarting or resuming the same delegation does not restore a removed watch.

tools.name: seed_unwatch
tools.title: remove this seed's subscription
tools.description: Removes this seed's subscription. It also drops a queued update only when the session is not a current tender, not a covering tender, and not covered by another watch. Separate child watches remain, and an ancestor watch can still cover the seed. `seed_show` and this command name those subscriptions and the commands that remove them.

seed.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

tools.name: seed_remind
tools.title: set a reminder that posts a message to the seed's mailbox
tools.description: Sets a reminder: at that time attn posts `message` to the seed's mailbox, which delivers it to whoever tends the seed then. When nobody tends it, the message waits for the next tender, who reads it with `attn agent inbox`. `in` counts from now; `at` takes an RFC3339 time; one of them is required unless `clear`. attn checks once a minute, so a message can arrive up to a minute late. A seed holds one reminder, and a new one replaces it. The reminder ends when attn posts the message, when `clear` removes it, and when the seed is harvested or withered. `seed_show` and `seed_ls` print it until then. While someone tends the seed, only the tender, sessions above it in the delegation chain, the profile's chief and the user can set or clear its reminder; anyone can while nobody holds the claim, and nobody can force it.

at.description: the time of the reminder, as an RFC3339 time such as 2026-11-05T09:00:00+01:00

in.description: how long from now until the reminder: 20m, 2h or 1h30m

message.description: the message to post; required unless --clear

seed.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

tools.name: seed_standby
tools.title: wait for seed mail with this session closed
tools.description:
Puts a seed you tend on standby with `next`, a note saying what to do next, and closes this session. When mail reaches the seed, attn resumes the session and delivers the note; for a crew member it starts a session. `in` and `at` also set the seed's reminder to that time, with the note as its message, as `seed_remind` does. When the session can compact, attn compacts it before closing; end your turn right after the command. `stay` keeps this session open.

attn refuses while the seed has mail you have not read; read it with `attn agent inbox` first. attn also refuses to close the session while it has an open ask, about this seed, another seed or none, and names each ask: a wait on the user keeps the session open, so ask with `attn ask` and end your turn. When the user tells you to close while an ask is open, put the seed on standby with `stay`, then run `attn agent close --self`: the seed stays on standby, and the answer resumes you.

Only the seed's tender sets standby, from its own session, and the seed stays claimed while the session is closed. A new standby replaces the note. Standby ends once you have read all of the seed's mail, and when the seed is parked, harvested, withered or gets a new tender. If the session closes before reading the mail, the mail resumes it again. `clear` ends standby and leaves the reminder.

at.description: also resume at this time, as an RFC3339 time such as 2026-11-05T09:00:00+01:00

in.description: also resume after this long: 20m, 2h or 1h30m

next.description: what to do when the session resumes; required unless --clear

seed.description: A seed's id, such as s-7k3f9m, or its slug. A slug two seeds share is refused, listing each match.

stay.description: keep this session open on standby

When someone other than the seed's tender changes the words, attn types the change into the tender's conversation as the user's message, waiting while the tender needs approval. With neither `words` nor `clear`, prints them and the state of the last typed update. Who may change them follows seed moves: the tender, sessions above it in the delegation chain, and the profile's chief; anyone in the profile while nobody holds the seed.

For a local file, `mode` is required: move transfers the file and leaves one editable canonical file, which is the recommended choice; copy keeps an independent source snapshot. Git-tracked files must use copy. A file the seed already has by that name is replaced, and `seed_show` marks check evidence replaced after its report; re-attaching an unchanged file changes nothing. A `path` in a `repo`, a `notebook` document and a `url` remain associations, and `note` goes on the log with them.

tools.description: Reads provider-neutral, timestamped, redacted conversation and tool events of one session. `after` resumes strictly after the cursor an earlier read ended on. `follow` keeps reading until interrupted; `--json` prints one event per line.

tools.name: session_list
tools.title: the session ledger, newest first, or every live session as a tree
tools.description:
Reads the session ledger, newest first: live sessions by default, `closed` for the ones that ended, `all` for both. When rows are omitted the notice names the id to pass to `before` for the next page. Filters combine and are applied before paging. `last` takes today, yesterday, 7d or 30d; `since` and `until` take a date or an RFC3339 instant and are half-open, so `until` excludes its own instant. `reopen` adds what would bring each closed row back, judging the whole page in one call; session_show explains any one of those verdicts.

`tree` shows every live session, and each closed agent on standby, nested under the session that dispatched it, sorted by label within each profile and branch. Rows carry short ids, agent, state, owed or snoozed turns and seed slugs. A delegate whose dispatcher is closed or absent becomes a root. A closed agent whose seed is on standby stays under its dispatcher with the state standby, and its seed column adds what it waits for. Shell split provenance is labeled separately. Inside attn the tree is limited to your session's profile; `profile` narrows it. Only `profile` goes with `tree`.

before.description: start after this session id, from a previous page's notice

profile.description: only sessions of this profile id, deleted profiles included

reopen.description: judge every closed row and add what would bring it back

repository.description: only sessions that ran in this repository path

since.description: only sessions from this date or RFC3339 instant onwards

tree.description: every live session, and each closed agent on standby, nested under its dispatcher

until.description: only sessions before this date or RFC3339 instant

tools.name: session_show
tools.title: one ledger row, live or closed, with who closed it and why
tools.description: Reads one ledger row, live or closed, including who closed it and why. A closed row also carries the reopen verdict: whether it comes back, why not when it does not, and the actions offered instead.

tools.name: session_priority
tools.title: mark a session so its owed turns go first, or clear the mark
tools.description: Marks a session so its owed turns go first, or clears that mark. `target` defaults to the session running this command. Any agent may mark any session.

priority.description: on marks the session, off clears the mark

target.description: the session to mark (defaults to the current session)

tools.name: session_snooze
tools.title: defer sessions' owed turns until a time
tools.description: Defers sessions until an RFC3339 instant, a positive duration (30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 8h), or tomorrow, saturday or monday. Day choices use local 09:00; quote a custom time, e.g. "tomorrow 09:00". A session may snooze itself and agents below it in its delegation chain, including delegates of delegates; the chief any session of its profile. Each id reports success or why it failed. session_unsnooze ends a snooze early.

tools.name: session_unsnooze
tools.title: end sessions' snoozes early
tools.description: Ends snoozes early, with the same permissions as session_snooze. Already unsnoozed is a successful no-op. session_list and session_show include the snoozed-until instant.

tools.name: session_rename

tools.description: Gives a session the name a person reads in the sidebar and the ledger: a few plain words about the work, up to 48 characters. `target` defaults to the session running this command. Rename when the main work drifts from the name it started with.

name.description: the new name; quote it when it has spaces

target.description: the session to rename (defaults to the current session)

tools.name: session_reopen
tools.title: bring a closed or stopped session back under its own id
tools.description: Brings a closed or stopped session back under its own id, on its last or current desktop in its profile. Without `action` it performs the plain reopen and refuses, naming what is offered, when the verdict does not allow one. Actions that recreate a worktree or fetch a branch write to the repository and only ever run when named here. Sessions whose profile was deleted cannot reopen. To close a session, use agent_close.

action.description: reopen, recreate_worktree_and_reopen or fetch_recreate_and_reopen; session_show lists the ones offered

tools.name: skill
tools.title: print the map of what attn can do, or a capability's rules
tools.description: Prints the map of what attn can do. `reference` prints one capability's rules instead, such as garden or delegation; read a capability's rules before you first use it. `list` prints the names of the bundled references, one per line. The text matches the running release.

reference.description: print this capability's rules, e.g. garden

tools.name: state_explain
tools.title: replay the recorded state observations of one session
tools.description: Replays the daemon's recorded state observations for one session: which source claimed what, and whether the claim was applied, vetoed before the store, discarded by it, or skipped by its own source. Identical observations in a row fold into one with a count. Reading it changes nothing.

id.description: the full id of the session to explain

tools.name: turn_open
tools.title: ask for the user; the turn opens when you stop
tools.description: Asks for the user. When a notification from attn started your run, your stop may not put you in the user's queue, so open your turn before you stop to bring them something you need or finished. Run while you work, it opens your turn when you stop, so the user is not sent to you while you are still busy. A later notification does not settle a turn you opened; the user does, or `turn_settle`. Use `ask` instead when you can keep working while the user decides.

tools.name: turn_settle
tools.title: settle a turn you opened, or cancel one that was going to open
tools.description: Settles a turn you opened, or cancels one that was going to open when you stop. A turn that opened when you stopped on your own is the user's to settle.

tools.name: vent
tools.title: record what got in your way; nobody replies
tools.description: Records a vent about attn's usability: an attn command that failed or behaved differently from its help or docs, attn instructions that contradict each other or attn's behavior, an attn capability you needed and had to work around, or attn not working inside your harness. With `about` tools, when the user turned tool vents on, it is about your other tooling instead: a skill, another CLI or MCP server, or your harness's permissions; the task and the repository are never tools. Don't vent because the work was hard, to report progress, or to ask for help. Say what happened, what you expected and what you did instead, in a paragraph at most. Nobody replies, so keep working. One vent per turn: to add to one, withdraw it with `vent_withdraw` and send one that covers both; withdraw a wrong vent instead of sending a correction.

about.description: What the vent is about: attn for attn itself, including attn blocked inside your harness, or tools for your other tooling (skills, other CLIs or MCP servers, harness permissions).

text.description: the vent, required; at most 16384 bytes

tools.name: vent_withdraw
tools.title: take back a vent you sent
tools.description: Takes back a vent this session sent.

vent.description: the vent's id, as recording it printed
